question: did anything published in the last five months change the conditions under which BAXY previously rejected an asset or runtime candidate?
method: primary sources only: the upstream issue that blocks MTP and the llama.cpp release feed. No asset was downloaded, no manifest was touched and no hash changed.

findings.subject: Gemma 4 E2B MTP assistant (previously rejected: acceptance 28.3%, chat +33%, outputs changed; and blocked on builds >= b9702)
findings.state: the issue is STILL OPEN. The regression that crashes the MTP draft during tensor loading between b9553 and b9702 has no linked fix or PR.
findings.verdict: rejection stands unchanged; no physical phase justified

findings.subject: llama.cpp runtime build
findings.state: upstream is at b10199 (2026-07-30); BAXY runs the registered b9980. The visible release notes cover server embeddings, Vulkan quantized concat, Metal memory and CUDA tuning. None of them mentions Gemma, speculative decoding, MTP, grammar/GBNF or prompt/KV cache reuse.
findings.verdict: no concrete hypothesis with expected value. Moving the registered runtime would change a productive asset and its hashes, which requires the full eight-gate promotion and explicit authorization; being N builds newer is not by itself a reason to open a physical phase.

conclusion: no candidate met the bar to open a physical measurement phase. The previous rejections (MTP, Ministral, Qwen3.5) remain valid and Gemma 4 E2B QAT remains canonical.
honesty_note: this revalidation checked the specific upstream blocker and the release feed. It is not an exhaustive survey of every quantized checkpoint published in the window.
